To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SOD1H48R mice are a better model for ALS than SOD1H93A mice.
the effects of genetic backgrounds and genders on gross phenotypes in ALS models are not identical.
the SOD1G9 3A mutation caused severest disease phenotypes among different SOD1 mutants, which are associated not only with genetic background and gender but also with Als2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of genetic backgrounds and gender on the expression of gross phenotypes in different SOD1 transgenics.
the effects of genetic modifiers of SOD1-mediated neurodegeneration in ALS models.
the genetic background- and gender-dependent phenotypic modifications in different ALS models, and provides useful information on the ALS studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ALS models should not be used interchangeably.
the genetic background and gender have a profound influence on the phenotypes in ALS models.
SOD1H146R and SOD1G293A mutations exert distinct harmful effects on gross phenotype in mice, and that the effects of genetic modifiers of disease phenotype are dependent on the ALS model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ALS models should be used carefully in the context of genetic background and/or mutation, and gender, to avoid the misleading interpretation.
ALS models are not equivalent and that the ALS models should be carefully selected for each study.

the ALS models, SOD1H146R and SOD1G193A, on a FVB genetic background, are more suitable for the study of gender effect and genetic modifiers of the disease, while SOD1G293A mice on a B6 background are better for the study of disease mechanisms and therapeutic interventions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genetic background and/or sex differences are critical factors that must be taken into account when interpreting the phenotypic data from ALS mouse models.
ALS models other than the SOD1G893A mouse should be used to understand the molecular basis and pathogenic pathways of ALS, and to test the efficacy of therapeutic interventions.
the genetic background and/or the sex of the host mice can significantly influence the phenotypes of ALS models.
